chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Jamhur, from his father, from his men, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who has a need for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, let him begin with the Salawat upon Muhammad and his Progeny, then he should ask his need, then he should conclude with the Salawat upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is more Benevolent than that He would accept the two ends and leave the middle, whenever there is Salawat upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, it is not blocked from Him.'

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: Salawat (blessings/prayer upon the Prophet and his family)
key_terms.الطَّرَفَيْنِ: The two ends (the beginning and ending Salawat)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended method for making a dua to ensure it is accepted according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi highlights the theological principle of 'tawassul' (seeking intercession) through the Prophet and his Ahl al-Bayt, framing Salawat not merely as ritual but as a spiritual conduit for divine acceptance. The metaphor of Allah being 'too generous to accept the two ends and leave the middle' underscores the certainty of the supplicant's request being granted when the medium of Salawat remains unobstructed by sin or heedlessness. This method reflects the Shia emphasis on the unique status of the Prophet's household as the primary means of drawing near to God.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Jamhour, from his father, from his man who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘The one who has a need for him to Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic, so let him begin with the Salawāt upon Muhammadsaww and hissaww Progenyasws, then he should ask his need, then he should end with the Salawāt upon Muhammadsaww and the Progenyasws of Muhammadsaww, for Allahazwj is more Benevolent than that Heazwj would Accept the two ends and Leave the middle. Whenever there was a Salawāt upon Muhammadsaww and the Progenyasws of Muhammad, it would never be Blocked from him’.
en.sarwar: 16. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from ibn Jumhur from his father from his narrators who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Whoever needs help from Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, should first ask from Allah al-Salat (favors) for the Holy Prophet and his family, then pray and plead before Allah for help, then conclude it with asking from Allah al-Salat for the Holy Prophet and his family; Honor of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, does not allow to accept both ends of the prayer and leave out the middle; asking from Allah al-Salat for the Holy Prophet and his family is never barred from reaching His presence.’”
